rules.name: Em dash
rules.message: The em dash reads as AI to many readers.
rules.why: Em dashes are a normal punctuation mark, but AI models use them so often that many readers now treat them as a sign of machine writing.
rules.fix: Use a comma, a colon or parentheses, or split the sentence in two.

flag: The plan worked — mostly.
pass: The plan worked, mostly.

rules.name: "Delve"
rules.message: "Delve" reads as AI.
rules.why: AI models use "delve" far more often than people do, so readers now link it to machine writing.
rules.fix: Try "look at", "dig into" or "explore".

flag: Let's delve into the numbers.
She delved deeper.
pass: Let's dig into the numbers.

rules.name: "It's not X, it's Y"
rules.message: The "it's not X, it's Y" setup reads as AI.
rules.why: Setting up a contrast just to knock it down is one of the most common AI sentence shapes. Readers spot it quickly.
rules.fix: Say the point directly: keep the Y part and drop the X part.

flag: It's not a tool, it's a movement.
This is not just about money; it's about trust.
pass: It's not ready yet, so we wait.

rules.name: "In today's fast-paced world"
rules.message: This opener reads as AI.
rules.why: Generic scene-setting openers are a classic sign of filler writing, and AI models reach for them constantly.
rules.fix: Start with your actual point or a specific fact.

flag: In today's fast-paced world, time is money.
In today’s digital landscape, brands must adapt.
pass: Today the store opens at nine.

rules.name: "Tapestry"
rules.message: "Tapestry" used as a metaphor reads as AI.
rules.why: Describing things as a "rich tapestry" is a favorite AI metaphor and rarely adds meaning.
rules.fix: Name the actual things you mean.

flag: The city is a rich tapestry of cultures.
pass: The museum restored a medieval rug.

rules.name: "A testament to"
rules.message: "A testament to" reads as AI.
rules.why: This phrase shows up constantly in AI writing to add weight without adding facts.
rules.fix: Say what the thing proves, with a specific detail.

flag: The award is a testament to our team's hard work.
pass: The team won the award after two years of work.

rules.name: "Navigate the landscape"
rules.message: "Navigate the landscape" reads as AI.
rules.why: Abstract travel metaphors like this are common in AI text and vague for readers.
rules.fix: Say what the person actually has to do.

flag: We help you navigate the complex landscape of taxes.
pass: We help you file your taxes on time.

rules.name: Hype words
rules.message: This hype phrase reads as AI.
rules.why: Big claims with no evidence are common in AI marketing copy. Readers skim past them.
rules.fix: Replace the claim with a number or a concrete result.

flag: This app is a game-changer for teams.
Unlock the full potential of your data.
pass: This app cut our meeting time in half.

rules.name: "Let's dive in"
rules.message: "Let's dive in" reads as AI.
rules.why: Announcing that you are about to start is filler, and AI models open with it all the time.
rules.fix: Delete it and start with the first real point.

flag: Let's dive into the details.
We'll jump right in.
pass: The details are below.

rules.name: Closing filler
rules.message: This stock phrase reads as AI.
rules.why: Stock openers and sign-offs are the first thing readers notice in AI emails and posts.
rules.fix: End with the next step or simply stop when you are done.

flag: I hope this helps!
In conclusion, the plan works.
pass: Call me Tuesday to confirm.

rules.name: Reveal setups
rules.message: This reveal setup reads as AI.
rules.why: Teasing a point before making it ("Here's the thing") is a common AI hook, especially on social media.
rules.fix: Make the point without the drumroll.

flag: Here's the thing: nobody reads the manual.
The kicker? It was free.
pass: Nobody reads the manual.

rules.name: Corporate buzzwords
rules.message: This buzzword reads as AI.
rules.why: These words are everywhere in AI business writing and say very little on their own.
rules.fix: Use a plain verb and say exactly what changes.

flag: Seamlessly integrate your tools.
Leverage our platform to grow.
pass: Connect your tools in two clicks.

rules.name: Stiff transition openers
rules.message: Opening with "Moreover" or "Furthermore" reads as AI.
rules.why: Formal transition words at the start of sentences are much more common in AI text than in natural writing.
rules.fix: Drop the transition, or use "Also" or "And".

flag: It is fast. Moreover, it is cheap.
Furthermore, the team agreed.
pass: It is fast and it is cheap.

rules.name: "It's worth noting"
rules.message: "It's worth noting that" reads as AI.
rules.why: This phrase adds words before the point without adding meaning. AI models use it constantly.
rules.fix: Delete the phrase and state the fact.

flag: It's worth noting that prices rose.
pass: Prices rose 4 percent in May.

rules.name: "Plays a crucial role"
rules.message: "Plays a crucial role" reads as AI.
rules.why: This is one of the most frequent AI phrases. It sounds important but hides what actually happens.
rules.fix: Say what the thing does, specifically.

flag: Sleep plays a crucial role in health.
pass: Sleep repairs muscle and fixes memories.

rules.name: "Certainly!"
rules.message: Opening with "Certainly!" reads as AI.
rules.why: Chat assistants start replies this way all the time. In an email or a post it sounds like a pasted chatbot answer.
rules.fix: Delete it and start with the answer.

flag: Certainly! Here is the list you asked for.
Absolutely! Let me explain.
pass: She will certainly be there on Friday.

rules.name: "Great question"
rules.message: "Great question!" reads as AI.
rules.why: Praising the question before answering it is a chatbot habit. Readers notice it right away.
rules.fix: Skip the praise and answer the question.

flag: Great question! The short answer is yes.
That's an excellent question.
pass: The great question of our time is energy.

rules.name: "As an AI"
rules.message: "As an AI" reads as a leftover from a chatbot reply.
rules.why: This phrase comes straight from chatbot answers. If it stays in your text, readers will assume the whole piece was pasted.
rules.fix: Delete the sentence, or rewrite it in your own voice.

flag: As an AI language model, I cannot give legal advice.
pass: As an artist, I see color everywhere.

rules.name: "It's important to remember"
rules.message: "It's important to remember" reads as AI.
rules.why: This hedge tells the reader something matters instead of showing why. AI models add it to almost every answer.
rules.fix: Drop the phrase and state the point. If it matters, the reason will show it.

flag: It's important to remember that every child is different.
It is crucial to keep in mind the budget.
pass: Remember to bring your ID.

rules.name: "Not only X but also Y"
rules.message: The "not only X but also Y" shape reads as AI when used often.
rules.why: People use this shape too, but AI text leans on it to sound balanced and thorough. Several in one piece stand out.
rules.fix: Try "X and Y", or give each point its own sentence.

flag: The app is not only fast but also secure.
pass: The app is fast and secure.
Not only that, it ships today.

rules.name: "In the realm of"
rules.message: "In the realm of" reads as AI.
rules.why: It is a grand way to say "in" and shows up far more in AI text than in normal writing.
rules.fix: Use "in" or name the field directly.

flag: In the realm of digital marketing, trust is key.
pass: The king ruled the realm for forty years.

rules.name: "Embark on a journey"
rules.message: "Embark on a journey" reads as AI.
rules.why: Turning a normal task into a journey is one of the most familiar AI metaphors.
rules.fix: Say what the person will actually do: "start", "learn", "try".

flag: Embark on a journey of self-discovery.
We embarked on an exciting new adventure.
pass: We boarded the ferry at noon.

rules.name: "Ever-evolving"
rules.message: "Ever-evolving" reads as AI.
rules.why: It is a stock way to sound current without saying what changed. AI models use it a lot.
rules.fix: Say what changed and when, or drop it.

flag: The ever-evolving world of tech moves fast.
An ever changing market needs new ideas.
pass: The market changed twice this year.

rules.name: "A myriad of"
rules.message: "A myriad of" reads as AI.
rules.why: Fancy words for "many" are common in AI text and make the sentence heavier.
rules.fix: Use "many", "lots of", or give the real number.

flag: The course covers a myriad of topics.
There is a plethora of options.
pass: The course covers twelve topics.

rules.name: "Foster a sense of"
rules.message: "Foster" in this sense reads as AI.
rules.why: AI writing loves to "foster" abstract things like community and growth. It sounds warm but says little.
rules.fix: Say what you do: "we meet weekly", "we answer every email".

flag: These events foster a sense of belonging.
We aim to foster collaboration.
pass: They foster kittens for the shelter.

rules.name: "Resonates with"
rules.message: "Resonates with" reads as AI.
rules.why: This is a common AI way to say people like something, without saying who or why.
rules.fix: Say who liked it and what they did: "readers shared it 200 times".

flag: This message resonates deeply with our audience.
pass: The bell resonated through the hall.

rules.name: "Unleash your potential"
rules.message: "Unleash your potential" reads as AI.
rules.why: This is a stock AI marketing line. Readers have seen it so often it no longer means anything.
rules.fix: Say the concrete result: what can the reader do after?

flag: Unleash your full potential with our app.
Unleash the power of AI.
pass: She unleashed the dog in the yard.

rules.name: "Harness the power of"
rules.message: "Harness the power of" reads as AI.
rules.why: This phrase is everywhere in AI product copy and hides what the product actually does.
rules.fix: Replace it with "use" and add what it does for the reader.

flag: Harness the power of data to grow your sales.
pass: Put the harness on the horse before the ride.

rules.name: "Imagine..." opener
rules.message: Opening with "Imagine..." reads as AI when overused.
rules.why: AI hooks often ask the reader to picture a scene before making the point. One is fine; a habit of it stands out.
rules.fix: Start with the real example or fact instead.

flag: Imagine a world where meetings end on time.
Picture it. Imagine waking up with no alarm.
pass: I can't imagine a better day.

rules.name: Emoji bullet headers
rules.message: Lines that start with emoji bullets read as AI.
rules.why: Stacks of lines that each begin with an emoji (🚀, ✅, 💡) are a common look in AI social posts.
rules.fix: Use plain bullets or short sentences. Keep an emoji only where it adds something.

flag:
🚀 Fast setup
✅ No code needed

💡 Tip one

🔥 Tip two
pass: We shipped it today 🚀

- Fast setup
- No code needed

rules.name: "Let that sink in"
rules.message: "Let that sink in" reads as AI.
rules.why: Telling readers to pause and be impressed is a worn-out social media line, and AI posts use it constantly.
rules.fix: Delete it. If the fact is striking, readers will notice on their own.

flag: Only 3 percent finish the course. Let that sink in.
pass: Let the paint dry overnight.

rules.name: "Read that again"
rules.message: "Read that again." reads as AI.
rules.why: This line tells the reader how to react instead of letting the point land. It is a common AI and engagement-bait habit.
rules.fix: Delete it and trust your point.

flag: You are not behind. Read that again.
pass: I read that again last night.

rules.name: "This changes everything"
rules.message: "This changes everything" reads as AI.
rules.why: Big claims with no proof are a hallmark of AI hype posts. Readers tune them out.
rules.fix: Say what changes, for whom, and by how much.

flag: A new model just dropped. This changes everything.
pass: This changes the schedule for Monday.

rules.name: Rule of three with abstract nouns
rules.message: A list of three abstract nouns reads as AI.
rules.why: AI text likes neat lists of three big ideas ("clarity, alignment and resilience"). They sound nice but are hard to picture.
rules.fix: Keep the one that matters most and give a concrete example.

flag: It brings clarity, alignment, and resilience.
We value innovation, excellence and commitment.
pass: We bought apples, bread, and milk.

rules.name: "Have you ever wondered"
rules.message: "Have you ever wondered" reads as AI.
rules.why: This question opener is a stock AI hook for blog posts and videos.
rules.fix: Start with the answer or the most interesting fact.

flag: Have you ever wondered why cats purr?
pass: I wondered why the cat was purring.

rules.name: "Let me know if you have any questions"
rules.message: This sign-off reads as AI.
rules.why: Chat assistants end nearly every reply with an offer to help more. In your own writing it sounds like a template.
rules.fix: End with a specific next step, or just stop.

flag: Let me know if you have any other questions!
I'd be happy to help with that.
pass: Let me know if Tuesday works.

rules.name: "Whether you're a X or a Y"
rules.message: "Whether you're a beginner or a pro" reads as AI.
rules.why: Trying to speak to everyone at once is a common AI opener. It makes the piece feel generic.
rules.fix: Pick the reader you are really writing for and speak to them.

flag: Whether you're a beginner or a pro, this guide helps.
pass: Whether it rains or not, we go.

rules.name: "Key takeaways"
rules.message: A "Key takeaways:" header reads as AI.
rules.why: AI summaries often end with a labeled list of takeaways, even in short posts that do not need one.
rules.fix: In short pieces, drop the header. The main point should already be clear.

flag: Key takeaways: sleep more and drink water.
pass: The key takeaway from the talk was simple.

rules.name: "In an era where"
rules.message: "In an era where" reads as AI.
rules.why: Sweeping openers about the times we live in are a classic AI way to start a paragraph.
rules.fix: Start with a specific fact about now instead.

flag: In an era where attention is scarce, brands must adapt.
In an age of noise, focus wins.
pass: The house was built in the era of steam.

rules.name: "The ultimate guide"
rules.message: "The ultimate guide" reads as AI.
rules.why: AI-written posts often call themselves the ultimate or comprehensive guide. Readers have learned to expect thin content.
rules.fix: Describe what the reader gets: "7 steps to set up your shop".

flag: This is the ultimate guide to email marketing.
A comprehensive guide to baking bread.
pass: The guide covers three trails near town.

rules.name: "The digital landscape"
rules.message: "The digital landscape" reads as AI.
rules.why: Calling a field a "landscape" is a favorite AI filler. It sounds big but points at nothing.
rules.fix: Name the actual market, tool or trend you mean.

flag: Brands must adapt to the digital landscape.
The competitive landscape is shifting.
pass: The landscape painting hangs in the hall.
